newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mecca pilgrims halts some Air India's German flights.
newsitem.headline: Mecca pilgrims halts some Air India's German flights.

text.p: Air India said it will suspend three of its five weekly Germany flights from March 8 in order to fly Moslem pilgrims to Saudi Arabia.
Air India Germany director P.P. Singh told Reuters: "This is because of the redeployment of part of the fleet to carry haj traffic."
The Indian government has told Air India to fly Moslems on the traditional haj pilgrimage to Mecca for the first time following tighter Saudi controls on foreign aircraft, airline sources said.
Singh said the three weekly direct Delhi-Frankfurt Boeing 747-200 flights will be suspended effective March 8 until the end of April, a reduction in passenger capacity of 25 percent.
"But we will still have two B747-400 flights a week on the Bombay-Frankfurt-Chicago route," he added.
Passengers have been re-booked on flights from other European cities or on other airlines, he said.
The four weekly flights to Paris would also be suspended with temporary cover through twice-weekly extension of London flights, Singh said.
